acceptance: TestRootSignalCenter_EveryCallSiteRoleIsAPublisherRole reads the roles from the call sites and fails on main naming integration, auth, queue, latency and retire
An integration-root emit reaches the root bus: a test attaches rootwire to a center of role integration in a temp evolve dir and reads the record back with source integration
fix: Register integration, auth, queue, latency and retire in publisher.Roles(), and update TestRoles_IsTheClosedSetOfTheSpecRoots and the event-channels spec role table. Replace the hand-written role list in the guard with the roles read from the call sites: the guard parses the first argument of each newRoleSignalCenter, newRoleSignalCenterWithAttach and newRootSignalCenter call in cmd/evolve, resolves a named constant through the package const declarations, and asserts each role is in publisher.Roles() and that the roles are distinct. Red first: the new guard fails on main with the 5 roles named.
summary: publisher.Roles() (go/internal/events/publisher/publisher.go:55-57) lists 15 roles. The CLI builds signal centers under 5 more: integration (cmd_integration_stop.go:19), auth (cmd_auth_seat_token.go:20), queue (cli_queue.go:33), latency (cmd_wave_latency_check.go:119) and retire (cmd_cycle_retire.go:66). Config.check (publisher.go:83-85) refuses each one, and rootwire.attach (go/internal/events/rootwire/rootwire.go:24-27) prints one stderr WARN and drops every event. Evidence on 2026-11-20: the 266 MB bus under .evolve/events/ch holds 0 records with source integration, auth, queue, latency or retire (wave 68, ship 18, quality 7387). The batch of PR #1600 printed '[events] WARN: role integration publishes no events', so the main-red stop release (GATE_REPO main-red release) and the batch hold signal were lost. The guard TestRootSignalCenter_EveryRootRunsUnderARoleOfTheClosedSet (go/cmd/evolve/cmd_root_guard_test.go:131-145) checks a hand-written list of 7 roles, not the roles that the call sites pass, so it stayed green when the 5 roots were added.
title: five signal roots run under roles that the publisher refuses, so their events never reach the bus
